title: Criminal background check for a Vietnam work permit (2026)
description: Which police check to order from 8 countries or Vietnam, what it costs, how to apostille it since 11 Sep 2026, and how to time it inside the 6-month limit.
h1: Criminal background check for a Vietnam work permit: which one, how to apostille it, and when to order it
intro: Vietnam's work permit needs a criminal record issued no more than 6 months before your employer files the dossier, from your home country or from Vietnam (Decree 219/2025/ND-CP). From the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa or the Philippines you order the national check, get one apostille in the issuing country and a certified translation in Vietnam; no Vietnamese embassy step since 11 September 2026. If you live here, the city police usually issue a Vietnamese record in 5 working days.
keyPoints: The 6 months run from the **issue date printed on the check to the day the dossier is filed** — not from the apostille date and not from your start date. A check that goes stale while the employer delays filing must be re-ordered.

Since 11 September 2026 Vietnam applies the Apostille Convention: US, UK, Canadian, Australian, Irish, New Zealand, South African and Philippine checks need **one apostille from the issuing country**, then a certified Vietnamese translation. German, Austrian and Czech checks still go through embassy legalisation.

Order the national, official check: FBI Identity History Summary (US$18), ACRO (listed at £70), RCMP fingerprint check (CAD 25 plus fingerprinting), AFP hard copy (A$57), Garda certificate (free), New Zealand Ministry of Justice record (free), SAPS clearance, NBI clearance.

Living in Ho Chi Minh City already? Ask HCMC Police for Phiếu lý lịch tư pháp số 1 at 161 Nguyễn Du (or the Thủ Dầu Một and Bà Rịa counters): {{vnd:200000}}, 5 working days as standard. The old Department of Justice counter no longer issues it.

You do not need a new check to extend your permit, or to move to a new employer in the same role while your permit is still valid. The move still needs a new permit, but since May 2026 neither case asks for your degree and experience proof again.

blocks.text: Work permits are governed by [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025; it replaced the foreign-worker rules of Decrees 152/2020 and 70/2023. Article 18(4) asks for a criminal record certificate, or a document confirming you are not serving a sentence, have no unexpunged conviction and are not being prosecuted. It may be issued **by a foreign country or by Vietnam**, and it must be issued no more than 6 months before the dossier is filed.

The clock starts on the issue date printed on the check and stops on the filing date. It does not restart when the check is apostilled or translated, and your start date does not matter. The one exception is the joint online route, where your employer applies for a Vietnamese record and the work permit together (see below), so no separate record is filed.

Your employer files, not you. Under the decree they file between 60 and 10 days before your start date, and the authority has up to 10 working days to decide; Ho Chi Minh City publishes 5 working days ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html)). In the city the Department of Home Affairs (Sở Nội vụ) issues permits for practically every language centre and school. The full dossier and process are in [our work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers); this page covers the police check only.

A foreign check must then be made usable in Vietnam. Decree 219 Article 5 asks for consular legalisation unless a treaty exempts the document, and Vietnam joined the [Apostille Convention](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41) with effect from 11 September 2026 under Decree 293/2026/ND-CP. Documents from member countries need an apostille; others still need consular legalisation. Either way, the document then needs a Vietnamese translation whose translator's signature is certified in Vietnam.

blocks.caption: Which route your police check takes, as of October 2026 (HCCH status table; Decree 293/2026/ND-CP; HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs notice of 11 September 2026)
headers: What it needs before use in Vietnam
rows: US, UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, the Philippines (and most other Convention members)
One apostille from the issuing country, then a certified Vietnamese translation. No Vietnamese embassy step.
Germany, Austria, Czechia
They objected to Vietnam's accession, so the old chain applies: home-country certification, then legalisation by the Vietnamese embassy or consulate, then a certified translation.
Thailand
Legalisation until the Convention takes effect for Thailand on 28 February 2027.
Vietnam
Nothing extra: a Vietnamese certificate is filed as it is.

blocks.text: The rules are national, but the authority that receives your dossier and your employer have the final word on what they will accept. Where this page says something is unclear, ask your employer and get the answer in writing before you order anything.

sections.title: Which check to order, country by country

blocks.text: Vietnam's decree does not name a product. It asks for a criminal record or confirmation from the competent authority, so order the national, official check from your country, ask for a **paper original** wherever the apostille office needs one, and do not laminate it. Fees below are in each country's own currency as of October 2026; the South African and Philippine fees could not be confirmed on official pages, so check the official page before paying.

blocks.text: United States: FBI report and State Department apostille

The [FBI Identity History Summary](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/more-fbi-services-and-information/identity-history-summary-checks/identity-history-summary-checks-faqs) is the national check. Fingerprints go on an FD-258 or FD-1164 card or are submitted electronically. The FBI says it authenticates results with its watermark and an official's signature at the time of submission and will not authenticate results processed earlier, so ask for the authenticated paper copy when you apply; the apostille needs that paper original. Because the report is federal, only the [State Department's Office of Authentications](https://travel.state.gov/en/replace-certify/authenticate-documents/request-services.html) can apostille it. **Do not have a notary stamp the FBI report first**; vendors report that this can make it ineligible.
United Kingdom: ACRO or Basic DBS

[ACRO](https://acro.police.uk/s/acro-services/police-certificates) is the UK's police certificate for people going to live or work abroad; extra copies are £7.75 and international courier £48. A [Basic DBS](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dbs-reduces-fees-for-checks-and-update-service-from-5-october-2026) is designed for jobs in England and Wales, and Scotland and Northern Ireland use other routes. Whether the Ho Chi Minh City office accepts a Basic DBS instead of ACRO is not documented, so ACRO is the safer choice unless your employer confirms the DBS in writing. Either way, the [FCDO](https://www.gov.uk/get-document-legalised) is the only UK apostille office, and British posts in Vietnam cannot legalise anything.
Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand

items: **Canada**: the [RCMP](https://rcmp.ca/en/criminal-records/criminal-record-checks/processing-times-and-fees) check is fingerprint-based; a name-only local police check is the weaker choice. Canada joined the Convention on 11 January 2024, and Global Affairs Canada apostilles federal documents such as RCMP checks.
**Australia**: the [AFP](https://afp.gov.au/our-services/national-police-checks) emails a secure PDF by default. The PDF cannot be apostilled: tick the hard-copy option when you apply.

**Ireland**: the [Garda certificate](https://www.garda.ie/en/about-us/online-services/data-protection-foi-police-certificates/police-certificates.html) is issued by the district where you live or lived; apply with the form, a certified copy of your passport or licence and proof of current and previous addresses. Garda says it is valid for 12 months, but Vietnam applies its own 6-month limit.

**New Zealand**: request your own record from the [Ministry of Justice](https://www.justice.govt.nz/criminal-records/get-your-own/) and send it to the DIA apostille service; any notarisation must be by a New Zealand notary public.

blocks.text: South Africa and the Philippines

South Africans have the tightest window: [DIRCO](https://dirco.gov.za/legalisation-services/) apostilles only an original SAPS clearance under 6 months old and stopped walk-ins on 1 September 2026, so book a slot as soon as the clearance arrives, or use a DIRCO-registered agent. Filipino teachers take the original NBI clearance to the [DFA apostille service](https://www.apostille.gov.ph/faqs/); photocopies are reportedly not accepted.

sections.title: From police check to a document Vietnam accepts

items.title: Order the national check, on paper
items.text: Use the official agency in the table above. Check that your name is spelled exactly as in your passport; if your name has changed, for example through marriage, apostille the marriage certificate or deed poll too.

items.title: Get the apostille in the issuing country
items.text: Send the original to the apostille office named above. Vietnamese embassies and consulates stopped legalising these documents on 11 September 2026 ([Decree 293/2026/ND-CP](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/293_2026_nd-cp_23072026_1-signed.signed.pdf) Article 37(1); the [Vietnamese Embassy in the USA](https://vietnamembassy-usa.org/news/2026/09/notice-application-apostille-place-consular-legalisation-11-september-2026) confirms it for US checks), so a quote that still includes a Vietnamese embassy attestation step for the eight countries in the table above is out of date. German, Austrian and Czech checks still take the legalisation chain.

items.title: Bring the original to Vietnam and keep scans
items.text: Carry the apostilled original in your hand luggage. Under [Decree 293/2026/ND-CP](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/293_2026_nd-cp_23072026_1-signed.signed.pdf) Vietnamese offices may not ask for legalisation on top of a valid apostille and can check it against the issuing country's online register or its QR code.

items.title: Translate it, including the apostille page
items.text: An apostille does not replace translation. Have the whole document translated into Vietnamese, apostille page included, after the apostille is attached. Since 1 July 2025 translations are made valid by certifying the translator's signature (chứng thực chữ ký người dịch) at any ward People's Committee or at a notary office ([Tạp chí Luật sư Việt Nam](https://lsvn.vn/se-khong-con-can-thuc-hien-cong-chung-ban-dich-tu-01-7-a159826.html)); the old notarised translation (công chứng bản dịch) no longer exists.

items.title: Hand it to your employer before the filing date
items.text: Give your employer the apostilled document and its certified translation, and confirm the date they will file. If a copy is filed instead of the original, Decree 219 requires the copy to be certified against the original before it is translated. An employer may not keep your original documents ([Labour Code Article 17](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html)), so get any original back once the dossier is in.

blocks.text: Who pays: the work permit's state fee in Ho Chi Minh City is {{vnd:600000}}, paid by the employer. In practice teachers usually pay for their own home-country documents, the apostilles and the courier. Translation and agent fees vary, so agree in writing who pays them; [our contracts guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam) covers what else to get in writing. Your degree and experience letters go through the same apostille-then-translate route, explained in [the degree authentication guide](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-your-degree-authenticated-for-vietnam).

sections.title: Already living in Vietnam: the Vietnamese criminal record (Phiếu lý lịch tư pháp)

blocks.text: Decree 219 accepts a Vietnamese record instead of a home-country one, and the law sets **no minimum stay**: any foreigner who has resided or is residing in Vietnam can request their own record from age 16 ([Ministry of Public Security](https://mps.gov.vn/chinh-sach-phap-luat/bai-viet/hoan-thien-hanh-lang-phap-ly-trong-cong-tac-quan-ly-va-cap-phieu-ly-lich-tu-phap-trong-tinh-hinh-moi-1774325375)). The often-repeated 6-month threshold comes from old labour-ministry guidance under earlier decrees. Whether a newly arrived teacher with no time in Vietnam can rely on a Vietnamese record alone is not settled, so ask your employer before skipping the home-country check.

Since 1 March 2025 these certificates are issued by the police, not by the Department of Justice (Sở Tư pháp); older guides that send you there, or to 258 Trần Hưng Đạo, are out of date. In Ho Chi Minh City, HCMC Police (Công an TP.HCM) take applications at three counters since 23 February 2026 ([Tuổi Trẻ](https://tuoitre.vn/cong-an-tp-hcm-thay-doi-dia-diem-tiep-nhan-va-tra-ket-qua-ly-lich-tu-phap-20260213171448319.htm)). Since July 2025 official addresses use the new ward names, so the counters are listed that way.

blocks.text: Bring your passport. Practitioner guides also say to bring proof that your address is registered with the local police, and report that foreigners' applications stall without it. Your landlord's residence declaration is what registers your address; it is covered in [our renting guide](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner). The [fee](https://baochinhphu.vn/tu-nay-den-31-12-2025-nop-ho-so-cap-phieu-ly-lich-tu-phap-truc-tuyen-duoc-giam-den-20-phi-102250424155449168.htm) is set by Circular 16/2025/TT-BTC; the online discount ended on 31 December 2025. Whether foreigners in the city can complete the request fully online in practice is not yet clear, so plan on the counter.
The joint online route through your employer

With your written authorisation, your employer can apply on the National Public Service Portal for the work permit and your Vietnamese record together (Decree 219 Article 6(3)). The police send an electronic certificate straight to the work-permit authority, both results come back to the employer electronically, and the processing time is the two procedures added together. Because no separate record is filed, the 6-month clock does not bite. The request goes to the police where you are registered as resident, so ask your employer early whether they use this route for someone in your situation.

If you later move on to a job in another country, the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Foreign Affairs at 6 Alexandre de Rhodes has apostilled Vietnamese documents, such as your Vietnamese record, since 11 September 2026: {{vnd:30000}} per copy, 1 working day for 1–4 documents ([HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs](https://mofahcm.gov.vn/so-ngoai-vu-thanh-pho-ho-chi-minh/thong-bao-ve-viec-tiep-nhan-ho-so-de-nghi-chung-nhan-apostilletai-bo-ngoai-giao)). The rest of the exit paperwork is in [the leaving checklist](/teach-in-vietnam/leaving-vietnam-checklist-for-teachers).

sections.title: Timing it so the check is still valid on the filing date

blocks.text: Work backwards from the filing date, not forwards from today. The employer files 60 to 10 days before your start date, and in practice you are usually in Vietnam by then, because the health certificate has to be done in Vietnam unless a mutual-recognition agreement applies. So the check has to survive the apostille queue, the post, your move and the translation, and still be under 6 months old when the employer files.

blocks.caption: Working backwards from a planned filing date (Decree 219 Articles 18 and 22; agency processing times above; practitioner advice)
rows: Before ordering
Have a signed offer and a target start date. Ask the employer for the planned filing date in writing and whether they want a home-country or a Vietnamese record
About 8–10 weeks before you need the apostilled document (UK providers' advice), longer for slow apostille queues
Order the check. Allow more for Canadian manual checks (up to 120 business days), Global Affairs Canada (about 25 business days) or a UK paper apostille (up to 25 working days)
As soon as the check arrives
Send it for the apostille; South Africans book DIRCO immediately because DIRCO will not apostille a clearance over 6 months old
After arrival
Translate it with the apostille page and have the translator's signature certified at a ward People's Committee or notary office
Filing date
The issue date on the check must be no more than 6 months earlier. If the start date slips, recheck the arithmetic

blocks.title: The check that goes stale
blocks.text: The most common way this fails: the check was issued early, the apostille or the job start was delayed, and by the filing date it is more than 6 months old, so the dossier is rejected. Count from the **issue date on the check**, not the apostille date. If your start date moves, work out the new filing date at once and re-order the check if it will be too old.

If you are still applying for jobs, do not order the check yet: with no filing date you cannot time it. The rest of the sequence, from offer to first lesson, is in [our step-by-step guide](/teach-in-vietnam/how-to-become-an-english-teacher-in-vietnam), and the [requirements guide](/teach-in-vietnam/requirements-to-teach-english-in-vietnam) lists every document the permit needs.

sections.title: Ordering a home-country check while you are in Vietnam

blocks.text: Teachers who arrived without their check, or who are changing route, can usually still order it from Vietnam. The catch is the apostille, which in most countries must be done at home by post or through an agent.

items: **United States**: the FBI check can be requested online or by mail, with fingerprints on an FD-258 or FD-1164 card; the State Department apostille is then done by mail.

**United Kingdom**: ACRO offers international courier for the certificate; the paper apostille must go to the FCDO in the UK by post or an agent, because British posts in Vietnam cannot legalise documents.

**Canada**: have ink fingerprints taken by local police or an authorised agency, then courier them to an RCMP-accredited fingerprinting company in Canada, which submits them electronically. Do not mail them to the RCMP; there are no accredited companies outside Canada.

**Australia**: order the AFP check online with a hard copy. DFAT accepts originals lodged at Australian embassies and consulates overseas, so ask the Consulate-General in Ho Chi Minh City whether it can process your apostille before you post anything home.

**Ireland and New Zealand**: the Garda certificate is applied for with the form, a certified copy of your passport or licence and proof of previous addresses, and the New Zealand record is requested online; both apostilles are handled at home.
**Any country**: a copy certified by your own consulate in Vietnam is a consular document outside the Apostille Convention, so it stays on the legalisation track rather than taking an apostille.

blocks.text: If you have lived in Vietnam, compare this with the Vietnamese record above: a counter in the city and about 5 working days is often simpler than an overseas apostille. If you have lived mainly in a third country, note that whether the city wants the check from your country of nationality or from your last country of residence is not published, so ask your employer which one they will file.

blocks.text: Changing employer always needs a new work permit, even for the same job ([Decision 526/QĐ-BNV](https://moha.gov.vn/Upload/a4c1b76d-88ab-49da-ac58-d23e8a518284Quyet%20dinh%20so%20526.QD-BNV.pdf)). Keep your apostilled originals and certified translations for every renewal and job change. If your case is anything other than the rows above, for example a different position, ask the new employer which route they will file and whether they need a fresh check.

A Ministry of Home Affairs draft amending Decree 219 would stop asking for documents already held in shared databases, such as criminal records. As of October 2026 it has not been issued, so the current rules above still apply.

faqs.a: In law, yes: Decree 293/2026 gives a foreign e-Apostille the same value as a paper one. How the Ho Chi Minh City work-permit office handles them day to day is not yet documented, and UK ACRO and DBS certificates cannot get an e-Apostille anyway, so a paper apostille on the original is the safer choice for a police check.

faqs.q: My police check was legalised by the Vietnamese embassy before 11 September 2026. Is it still valid?
faqs.a: The legalisation stays valid and no office may demand an apostille on top of it. The 6-month rule still applies, though: if the check was issued more than 6 months before the filing date, you need a new one.

faqs.q: I am German, Austrian or Czech. Can I use an apostille?
faqs.a: No. Germany, Austria and Czechia objected to Vietnam's accession, so the Convention does not apply between them and Vietnam. Your check needs certification at home, then legalisation by the Vietnamese embassy or consulate, then a certified Vietnamese translation.

faqs.q: What if my record is not clean?
faqs.a: The Labour Code requires that a foreign worker is not serving a sentence, has no unexpunged conviction and is not being prosecuted. How a particular foreign conviction is treated is a question for a Vietnamese lawyer and your employer, so raise it before you resign or travel, not after.

faqs.q: Do I need a translation if my police check is already in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Every foreign document in a work-permit dossier needs a Vietnamese translation with the translator's signature certified in Vietnam, and the translation should cover the apostille page as well.

faqs.q: Can I walk into the Department of Justice (Sở Tư pháp) for a Vietnamese record?
faqs.a: No. Since 1 March 2025 the provincial police issue criminal records. In Ho Chi Minh City go to HCMC Police at 161 Nguyễn Du, 681 Cách Mạng Tháng 8 (Thủ Dầu Một) or 4 Nguyễn Tất Thành (Bà Rịa).
